item.title: Researchers Propose Hybrid Artificial Intelligence Architecture to Optimize Complex Pharmacotherapy Regimens - Bioengineer.org
item.description:
요약

  • An interdisciplinary research group has formulated a conceptual framework designed to optimize pharmacotherapy in multimorbid patients through a clinician-supervised hybrid artificial intelligence system.
  • The development, published in the International Journal of Clinical Pharmacy, responds to the increasing clinical complexity driven by polypharmacy, fragmented patient records, expanding electronic health records, drug shortages, and healthcare workforce constraints.
  • The conceptual framework was formulated between June 2025 and February 2026 by an interdisciplinary team comprising specialists in clinical pharmacy, pharmacotherapy, artificial intelligence, digital health, and medication management.

본문

An interdisciplinary research group has formulated a conceptual framework designed to optimize pharmacotherapy in multimorbid patients through a clinician-supervised hybrid artificial intelligence system. The development, published in the International Journal of Clinical Pharmacy, responds to the increasing clinical complexity driven by polypharmacy, fragmented patient records, expanding electronic health records, drug shortages, and healthcare workforce constraints. Clinicians routinely face mounting time pressure when evaluating intricate medication regimens, while conventional clinical decision support systems remain primarily static and rule-based. These legacy systems frequently emit non-contextual alerts that cause alert fatigue and exhibit limited clinical utility. By combining structured clinical records, patient-specific context, and deterministic safety mechanisms, the newly proposed architecture establishes an analytical layer intended to support rather than replace human clinical judgment in high-risk therapeutic environments.

The conceptual framework was formulated between June 2025 and February 2026 by an interdisciplinary team comprising specialists in clinical pharmacy, pharmacotherapy, artificial intelligence, digital health, and medication management. Rather than executing a formal consensus methodology or clinical trial, the authors adopted a design science-informed approach guided by problem identification, artifact design, and iterative refinement. The investigative process was directly informed by earlier feasibility work in artificial intelligence-supported pharmacotherapy, existing literature examining clinical decision support platforms, and recurrent challenges observed in clinical practice. The resulting conceptualization positions hybrid artificial intelligence not as an autonomous prescriber, but as a specialized decision-support infrastructure engineered to structure clinical relevance, reduce cognitive burden, and safeguard interprofessional decision-making.

A foundational premise of the research is that stand-alone artificial intelligence models, especially general-purpose large language models, remain insufficiently reliable when deployed independently in complex medication management. While large language models demonstrate utility in answering isolated biomedical inquiries and categorizing descriptive data, they present substantial clinical risks when functioning without structured clinical context, verification mechanisms, and explicit justifications. To counteract these operational limitations, the researchers defined hybrid artificial intelligence as an operational integration uniting three distinct computational mechanisms: retrieval-augmented generation, deterministic safety rules, and contextual large language model reasoning. This structural combination grounds model responses in validated external medical evidence while enforcing deterministic boundaries against unsafe therapeutic recommendations.

item.title: Modified Technology Acceptance Model Accurately Evaluates Hospital Physician E-Consultation Adoption - Bioengineer.org
item.description:
요약

  • A newly adapted psychometric instrument based on the Technology Acceptance Model provides a statistically reliable and structurally valid method for evaluating how hospital physicians perceive and adopt remote electronic consultation platforms.
  • The expansion of digital health infrastructure has become an essential strategy for international healthcare systems striving to optimize specialized clinical delivery and advance health equity in geographically isolated and under-resourced regions.
  • The World Health Organization has identified electronic consultation as a cost-effective, secure modality that facilitates clinical communication, professional medical education, and collaborative patient care across institutional boundaries.

본문

A newly adapted psychometric instrument based on the Technology Acceptance Model provides a statistically reliable and structurally valid method for evaluating how hospital physicians perceive and adopt remote electronic consultation platforms. Developed and evaluated within the public healthcare infrastructure of the Egyptian Ministry of Health and Population, the modified questionnaire demonstrated robust internal consistency and clear structural dimensionality when administered to medical practitioners receiving virtual specialist input. The validation analysis confirmed that the measurement tool accurately captures two distinct primary domains: perceived usefulness and perceived ease of use. By establishing strong internal reliability coefficients exceeding 0.92 across both domains and verifying the structural fit through advanced latent variable modeling, the investigation offers healthcare administrators a verified mechanism for diagnosing adoption barriers, assessing clinician satisfaction, and guiding future implementations of digital consultation workflows in resource-constrained hospital environments.

The expansion of digital health infrastructure has become an essential strategy for international healthcare systems striving to optimize specialized clinical delivery and advance health equity in geographically isolated and under-resourced regions. The World Health Organization has identified electronic consultation as a cost-effective, secure modality that facilitates clinical communication, professional medical education, and collaborative patient care across institutional boundaries. In Egypt, early limited-scale deployments mirrored similar initiatives across developing digital ecosystems, including programs established in Saudi Arabia, China, and India. The operational landscape shifted dramatically following the global outbreak of the COVID-19 pandemic in 2020, during which public quarantine facilities relied on virtual consultations to coordinate multidisciplinary patient management while mitigating contagion risks. Following that acute crisis, institutional utilization data prompted the Egyptian Ministry of Health and Population to double its operational footprint from 150 to 300 specialized e-consultation units across 26 national governorates, completing more than 27,000 formal clinical teleconsultations by late 2022, primarily concentrated in dermatology, internal medicine, and pediatrics.

item.title: 복지부·진흥원, 미국 헬스 유에스에이 2026 디지털헬스케어 한국관 운영 - MEDI:GATE NEWS
item.description:
요약

  • 보건복지부와 한국보건산업진흥원은 지난 15일부터 18일까지 미국 라스베이거스 베네시안 엑스포 센터에서 열린 '헬스 유에스에이(HLTH USA) 2026'에서 '디지털헬스케어 한국관'을 운영했다고 밝혔다.
  • 헬스 유에스에이는 의료기관, 보험사, 제약사, 투자사 등 헬스케어 산업 전반의 의사결정권자가 모이는 미국 최대 규모의 디지털 헬스케어 혁신 행사다.
  • 진흥원에 따르면 이번 한국관에는 디지털 치료, 인공지능(AI) 진단, 만성질환 관리 등 분야의 디지털헬스케어 기업 9개사가 참여했다.

본문

보건복지부와 한국보건산업진흥원은 지난 15일부터 18일까지 미국 라스베이거스 베네시안 엑스포 센터에서 열린 '헬스 유에스에이(HLTH USA) 2026'에서 '디지털헬스케어 한국관'을 운영했다고 밝혔다. 헬스 유에스에이는 의료기관, 보험사, 제약사, 투자사 등 헬스케어 산업 전반의 의사결정권자가 모이는 미국 최대 규모의 디지털 헬스케어 혁신 행사다. 올해 행사 주제는 '지능형 헬스케어의 시대'였다. 진흥원에 따르면 이번 한국관에는 디지털 치료, 인공지능(AI) 진단, 만성질환 관리 등 분야의 디지털헬스케어 기업 9개사가 참여했다. 행사 기간 총 195건의 비즈니스 상담을 진행했으며, 계약 3건, 현지 실증(PoC) 2건, 업무협약(MOU) 및 공동 연구개발(R&D) 협력 2건의 성과를 거뒀다. 진흥원은 올해 한국관 규모를 전년 대비 2배 이상 확장했다. 현장에서는 기업별 홍보·상담 공간(부스) 운영, 해외 시장·투자자 연계 프로그램(마켓 커넥트·인베스터 커넥트) 지원, 현장 구매자(바이어) 1대1 상담 등을 지원했다. 진흥원은 미국 내 판로를 개척하고 한국 디지털헬스케어의 브랜드 인지도를 높이기 위해 한국관 운영을 기획했다고 설명했다. 참여 기업과 주요 제품은 웰트(불면증 디지털치료기기), 이삼사일(비만치료제(GLP-1) 관리 플랫폼), 링키스(인공지능 의료상담 플랫폼), 넥스브이(인공지능 정신건강 키오스크), 브이에스아이(휴대용 엑스레이(X-ray), 한국신체정보원(인공지능 근골격계 진단장치), 어반데이터랩(디지털병리 통합 플랫폼), 가시안(인공지능 사물인터넷(AIoT) 기반 스마트 약통, 에스디씨 웰케어(만성 대사질환 조기선별 솔루션) 등 총 9개사 제품이다. 진흥원 한동우 국제의료본부장은 "AI가 핵심 화두가 된 올해 행사에서 국내 기업들이 글로벌 파트너들의 큰 관심을 이끌어냈다"며 "진단·치료·관리 전 분야에서 우리 기업들의 존재감을 보여준 자리였다"고 말했다. 이어 "진흥원은 우리 기업들이 미국 시장에 안정적으로 안착할 수 있도록 현지 네트워크를 넓히고 후속 협력을 지속 지원하겠다"고 밝혔다.

item.title: Digital Platforms Give Consumers a Map to Navigate New Ways to Access Medicines - MedCity News
item.description:
요약

  • Consumer choice for filling a prescription used to be selecting which pharmacy to go to. Patients still have that option, of course.
  • “We really see this as a clear need in this industry to put more agency at the patient and the members’ hands to see what their options are and make the best decision for them,” Baynes said.
  • Baynes said innovation in consumer offerings can also come by making the journey easier for patients to navigate so they don’t get to the pharmacy counter only to find a drug is unavailable or is not covered.

본문

Consumer choice for filling a prescription used to be selecting which pharmacy to go to. Patients still have that option, of course. But choice now extends to new online offerings fulfilled by home delivery. Behind the scenes, the companies supporting these digital options are working to ensure a user’s experience is as seamless and straightforward as possible.

The growth of consumer platforms for medicines was the topic of a panel discussion during MedCity News’ recent INVEST Digital Health Conference in Dallas. The panel was moderated by Shelley Bailey of the Independent Pharmacy Cooperative.

Pharmacies are still the place where consumers most frequently interact with the healthcare system. But Bethanie Baynes, director of payer relations & business development, Amazon Pharmacy, said pharmacies have historically offered little transparency about what is covered, how much something will cost, and whether they have other options.

“We really see this as a clear need in this industry to put more agency at the patient and the members’ hands to see what their options are and make the best decision for them,” Baynes said.

Michelle Davey, CEO of care orchestration company Wheel, said that when her company started in 2018, most of the discussion around consumer healthcare was about cash pay interactions. Today, it’s not just about payment methods, it’s about pricing transparency and helping consumers understand their benefit information, including the cost of paying cash versus using insurance. Patients need support through the entire healthcare journey, not just one particular point of that journey, Davey said. This more holistic view helps patients come back and continue to use the digital tools.

Point of care does not end with a single interaction, Davey said. Beyond follow-up visits, there is a need to ensure adherence to medication. The goal is to ensure patients get the care they need in the moment as well as over time. Achieving that goal requires integration and connection of the disparate pieces of the healthcare system.

Right now, there are many channels where a prescription can be filled, dispensed, and received by the consumer, patient, or insurance plan member, said Jessin Joseph, vice president, PBA markets, at Judi Health, a pharmacy benefit administrator and medical claim adjudication platform. Historically, the different pieces of the system, such as pharmaceutical companies and the pharmacy benefit managers, have been siloed. Judi is trying to reduce the heavy lifting for patients, enabling them to see where a drug can be dispensed and how much those options will cost. The key is integrating this information with a patient’s pharmacy benefit.

“At the end of the day, there’s no reason why people have to go to every different pharmacy to figure out what is the cost of the drug,” Joseph said.

item.title: Health Systems Are Incubating Startups - Fitt Insider
item.description:
요약

  • Launching venture studios and funds, health systems are backing answers to their own problems.
  • Following a merger with Sheba Medical Center’s innovation arm ARC, Redesign Health launched a Growth Equity practice focused on healthcare IT, AI-enabled services, and clinical AI — making minority investments from Series A through pre-IPO.
  • Combining Atrium Health and Wake Forest University’s clinical expertise with Eshelman Innovation’s venture-building network, Atrium’s new NC-based digital health venture studio will guide select startups on a six-month sprint.

본문

Launching venture studios and funds, health systems are backing answers to their own problems.

Kaiser. A subsidiary of The Permanente Medical Group, Permanentech is Kaiser’s physician-led innovation firm. Its first portco, Wrapt Health, uses AI to predict missed appointments.

Redesign. Following a merger with Sheba Medical Center’s innovation arm ARC, Redesign Health launched a Growth Equity practice focused on healthcare IT, AI-enabled services, and clinical AI — making minority investments from Series A through pre-IPO.

Aegis Digital Consortium. Aegis Ventures works with a coalition of health systems including Northwell Health, Stanford Health Care, and Vanderbilt Health to co-develop and deploy tech. With six companies launched and >$200M raised, its portfolio includes innovations like Wavelet’s EEG-based fetal brain monitoring platform.

Atrium. Combining Atrium Health and Wake Forest University’s clinical expertise with Eshelman Innovation’s venture-building network, Atrium’s new NC-based digital health venture studio will guide select startups on a six-month sprint.

Takeaway: Turning operational pain points into venture opportunities, health systems are using existing clinical infrastructure as both testing ground and go-to-market advantage.

item.title: Half Of Surveyed Egyptian University Physicians Use Telemedicine Despite Infrastructure Obstacles - Bioengineer.org
item.description:
요약

  • By investigating both healthcare providers and institutional employees, the published findings deliver empirical insights into how clinical specialists and administrative consumers navigate digital health platforms within an evolving national medical infrastructure.
  • To compensate for incomplete submissions and enhance validity, researchers expanded the target by 20 percent to 941 participants, distributing 1,050 questionnaires through convenience sampling across operational working hours.
  • Knowledge, attitude, and practice regarding telemedicine among physicians and employees at Tanta University Hospitals, Egypt. Journal of the Egyptian Public Health Association, 100(1), Article 13. https://doi.org/10.1186/s42506-025-00194-y

본문

At the medical campus of Tanta University in Egypt, a cross-sectional investigation conducted between November 2023 and March 2024 revealed that half of surveyed physicians and 38.2 percent of administrative employees actively utilize telemedicine and electronic health platforms in their everyday healthcare interactions. The research team surveyed one thousand participants operating within an expansive academic healthcare network located in the Middle Nile Delta, an institutional complex serving an estimated catchment population of eighteen million patients annually across hospital departments and academic faculties. The study evaluated foundational knowledge, professional attitudes, and direct practical implementations of digital healthcare delivery, seeking to illuminate user perspectives within Egyptian university medical environments where remote clinical tools expanded during the COVID-19 pandemic. By investigating both healthcare providers and institutional employees, the published findings deliver empirical insights into how clinical specialists and administrative consumers navigate digital health platforms within an evolving national medical infrastructure.

Digital healthcare encompasses a multidisciplinary convergence of technological capabilities and clinical delivery models, incorporating specialized software applications, interactive hardware systems, wearable physiological sensors, electronic health records, and structured telemedicine frameworks. The World Health Organization defines telemedicine as the delivery of healthcare services where physical distance represents a critical factor, conducted by healthcare professionals utilizing information and communication technologies to exchange valid clinical data for diagnosis, therapeutic intervention, injury prevention, ongoing research, and provider education. While traditional healthcare delivery systems in developing nations confront mounting resource constraints, escalating operational expenditures, and rising clinical demands, remote technological platforms offer viable pathways toward expanding primary clinical access and specialized expertise. In Egypt, strategic investments in information society frameworks and specialized digital initiatives, such as the national Be He@lthy Be Mobile diabetes project launched in 2015 and the government electronic mental health counseling platform introduced in 2022, have steadily advanced digital care delivery across diverse geographic sectors.

item.title: Digital Therapy Improves Quality of Life for Half of Osteoarthritis Patients - Bioengineer.org
item.description:
요약

  • The investigation, which evaluated clinical outcomes documented in the Joint Academy registry, tracked changes in health profiles using the standardized five-level EuroQol five-dimensional questionnaire, known as the EQ-5D-5L.
  • Osteoarthritis represents the most prevalent form of arthritis globally and serves as a primary cause of physical functional limitations and enduring pain.
  • Article Title: Changes in health-related quality of life: a longitudinal registry study among over 15,000 participants of a digital education and exercise therapy for knee and hip osteoarthritis using EQ-5D-5L

본문

A large descriptive longitudinal registry study following more than 15,000 participants in Sweden has found that approximately half of patients undergoing a smartphone-delivered education and exercise program for knee and hip osteoarthritis experienced improvements in their overall health-related quality of life over three- and twelve-month periods. The investigation, which evaluated clinical outcomes documented in the Joint Academy registry, tracked changes in health profiles using the standardized five-level EuroQol five-dimensional questionnaire, known as the EQ-5D-5L. While the findings provide broad real-world evidence supporting the reach of first-line nonpharmacological management through digital applications, the data also revealed marked divergence in patient trajectories, with one in five participants reporting worse overall health profiles and substantial proportions experiencing no relief from persistent joint discomfort.

Osteoarthritis represents the most prevalent form of arthritis globally and serves as a primary cause of physical functional limitations and enduring pain. Because no medical cure exists for the chronic condition, treatment guidelines prioritize core first-line interventions focused on patient education, structured exercise regimens, and weight control. The primary goal of these strategies is to alleviate pain, maintain physical mobility, and bolster health-related quality of life across physical, mental, and social domains. In recent years, healthcare delivery systems have substantially expanded digital platforms to deliver these core therapies directly to individuals outside traditional clinical environments. However, previous assessments of digital education and physical programs have relied predominantly on smaller randomized controlled trials with brief follow-up intervals, leaving questions about the sustained real-world impact across larger, clinically diverse patient populations.

The study cohort analyzed consecutive adults aged 40 years and older who enrolled in the Swedish digital intervention between January 1, 2019, and September 30, 2021, and provided digital consent for research. The digital program delivered structured instructional video lectures covering osteoarthritis pathology, physical self-management, and activity guidelines, accompanied by daily individualized exercise routines adjusted dynamically to user progression via a smartphone interface. Participants also received regular clinical supervision from physical therapists through secure telephone or video consultations, supplemented by continuous asynchronous text communication. While users had the option to extend participation indefinitely, the foundational clinical curriculum and core exercise package were administered over the initial 12 weeks of enrolment.

item.title: Digital Health Maturity Links to Patient Trust Through Transparency and Coordination - Bioengineer.org
item.description:
요약

  • Perceived digital health service maturity does not directly ensure patient satisfaction but connects to patient trust through the distinct operational experiences of service transparency and care coordination, according to an observational study in Frontiers in Public Health.
  • The investigation differentiated institutional digital adoption—such as online appointment portals, electronic health records, and communication tools—from the subjective patient experience of whether those platforms render medical care understandable, predictable, and seamless.
  • The largest observed ratio was 0.770 between care coordination and patient trust, followed by 0.761 between transparency and coordination, 0.751 between transparency and trust, and 0.737 between trust and satisfaction.

본문

Perceived digital health service maturity does not directly ensure patient satisfaction but connects to patient trust through the distinct operational experiences of service transparency and care coordination, according to an observational study in Frontiers in Public Health. Investigating how patients evaluate healthcare technologies, researcher Kadriye Sönmez from Istanbul Topkapi University analyzed survey responses from adults reporting recent healthcare use across Istanbul, Türkiye. The investigation differentiated institutional digital adoption—such as online appointment portals, electronic health records, and communication tools—from the subjective patient experience of whether those platforms render medical care understandable, predictable, and seamless. Rather than demonstrating an immediate direct link between advanced digital features and ultimate patient satisfaction, latent structural equation models indicated that digital maturity operates through interrelated perceptions of process clarity and coordinated handoffs. These findings indicate that technological capability alone cannot secure patient confidence unless digital systems actively illuminate care pathways and support continuous service delivery across units.

The research established strict conceptual boundaries among several patient-reported dimensions often conflated in institutional healthcare evaluations. Perceived digital service maturity was defined specifically as the patient appraisal of digital channel accessibility, operational reliability, user convenience, and cross-channel integration during a recent care episode, rather than an objective institutional accreditation or hospital technology score. Alongside digital maturity, the study evaluated service transparency, which captures the intelligibility of care processes, including explicit timelines, communication of procedural changes, visibility of professional responsibilities, and clear explanations regarding how patient data are utilized. Care coordination was specified as the perceived continuity and consistency of clinical information, referrals, and medical handoffs across units without redundant data collection. Patient trust and patient satisfaction were modeled as distinct evaluative endpoints, recognizing that while trust reflects institutional confidence under conditions of vulnerability, satisfaction represents a retrospective appraisal combining interpersonal expectations and overall treatment experiences.

item.title: Public Health Engagement Must Move Beyond Reactive Misinformation Debunking in Africa - Bioengineer.org
item.description:
요약

  • Authored by Emmanuel Twumasi, Matilda Essuman, and Albert Asare Adu, the paper examines how the rapid expansion of mobile broadband and social media platforms—including WhatsApp, TikTok, X, and Facebook—has reshaped health information environments.
  • The perspective situates digital misinformation within a broader social and historical framework, highlighting that rumors, inaccurate health beliefs, and skepticism toward official messaging have complicated epidemic responses long before the advent of the internet.
  • Combining digital social listening with community-based qualitative inquiry ensures that public health analysts can distinguish the mere volume of rapidly circulating online claims from the actual knowledge, beliefs, and lived realities of affected populations.

본문

A perspective published in Discover Public Health argues that public health institutions responding to disease outbreaks across Africa must transition away from purely reactive, centralized debunking and technological surveillance toward integrated, participatory public engagement. Authored by Emmanuel Twumasi, Matilda Essuman, and Albert Asare Adu, the paper examines how the rapid expansion of mobile broadband and social media platforms—including WhatsApp, TikTok, X, and Facebook—has reshaped health information environments.

Over the past decade, increasing mobile connectivity across sub-Saharan Africa has positioned digital platforms as vital complements to traditional risk communication channels. However, these platforms simultaneously permit inaccurate and misleading health claims to circulate rapidly during public health crises. Rather than treating misinformation as an independent driver of adverse population behavior, the authors stress that empirical research consistently identifies associations between misinformation exposure and attitudes such as vaccine hesitancy and institutional distrust, rather than direct causal effects. Importantly, recent population-based findings indicate that misinformation endorsement and recommended health practices frequently coexist, as many individuals who express belief in vaccine-related misinformation nevertheless accept vaccination.

The perspective situates digital misinformation within a broader social and historical framework, highlighting that rumors, inaccurate health beliefs, and skepticism toward official messaging have complicated epidemic responses long before the advent of the internet. Digital networks alter the velocity, reach, visibility, persistence, and potential amplification of claims, yet digital platforms function merely as additional channels within a wider ecosystem rather than the original genesis of false beliefs. Furthermore, the authors cite analyses from the 2014 West African Ebola epidemic demonstrating that while misinformation was present on social networks, it accounted for a relatively small proportion of sampled online content, with community rumors circulating extensively via offline and interpersonal networks.

Traditional risk communication during health emergencies is frequently weakened by institutional paternalism and an unwillingness to acknowledge scientific uncertainty. When public health authorities delay advisories until data collection is complete or portray shifting, preliminary evidence as definitive fact, they inadvertently create communication vacuums. These voids are readily filled by speculation, unverified alternative therapies, and conspiracy theories. To avoid these pitfalls, the authors contend that health security frameworks must pay equal attention to the social, cultural, and institutional contexts that govern how communities encounter, evaluate, accept, or dismiss health information.
